import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Filter for the latest available year to get a single snapshot of the dog population
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest_year = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# For breeds, handle 'Unbekannt' or NaN values
df_latest_year['Rasse1Text'].fillna('Unbekannt', inplace=True)
# Filter out 'Unbekannt' for the top breeds visualization, as it's not a specific breed
df_known_breeds = df_latest_year[df_latest_year['Rasse1Text'] != 'Unbekannt']

# Set a consistent style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 7)) # Adjust figsize as needed

# --- Visualization 1: Top 10 Dog Breeds ---
top_breeds = df_known_breeds['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10)
sns.barplot(x=top_breeds.values, y=top_breeds.index, palette='viridis', ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title(f'Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)

# --- Visualization 2: Distribution of Dogs by District and Gender ---
# Count dogs per district and gender
district_gender_counts = df_latest_year.groupby(['KreisLang', 'SexHundLang']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Define a desired order for gender columns for consistent stacking
desired_gender_order = ['männlich', 'weiblich', 'unbekannt']
# Filter for existing columns and reindex to ensure desired order
existing_gender_columns = [g for g in desired_gender_order if g in district_gender_counts.columns]
district_gender_counts = district_gender_counts[existing_gender_columns]

# Plotting stacked bar chart
district_gender_counts.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, color=sns.color_palette("pastel", n_colors=len(existing_gender_columns)), ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title(f'Dog Distribution by District and Gender in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('District', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right', labelsize=10)

axes[1].legend(title='Dog Gender', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Filter for the latest available year to get a single snapshot of the dog population
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest_year = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# For breeds, handle 'Unbekannt' or NaN values
df_latest_year['Rasse1Text'].fillna('Unbekannt', inplace=True)
# Filter out 'Unbekannt' for the top breeds visualization, as it's not a specific breed
df_known_breeds = df_latest_year[df_latest_year['Rasse1Text'] != 'Unbekannt']

# Set a consistent style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 7)) # Adjust figsize as needed

# --- Visualization 1: Top 10 Dog Breeds ---
top_breeds = df_known_breeds['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10)
sns.barplot(x=top_breeds.values, y=top_breeds.index, palette='viridis', ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title(f'Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)

# --- Visualization 2: Distribution of Dogs by District and Gender ---
# Count dogs per district and gender
district_gender_counts = df_latest_year.groupby(['KreisLang', 'SexHundLang']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Define a desired order for gender columns for consistent stacking
desired_gender_order = ['männlich', 'weiblich', 'unbekannt']
# Filter for existing columns and reindex to ensure desired order
existing_gender_columns = [g for g in desired_gender_order if g in district_gender_counts.columns]
district_gender_counts = district_gender_counts[existing_gender_columns]

# Plotting stacked bar chart
district_gender_counts.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, color=sns.color_palette("pastel", n_colors=len(existing_gender_columns)), ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title(f'Dog Distribution by District and Gender in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('District', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right', labelsize=10)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)
axes[1].legend(title='Dog Gender', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
